title: Decompression and Decompression Sickness
note: Mahon and Regis 2014, PMID 24944033. User-supplied 19-page review. OpenAlex W1491023115 has alternate indexed DOI 10.1002/j.2040-4603.2014.tb00566.x. No independent outcome cohort.

title: Twelve Year Survey of the Susceptibility of Women to Altitude Decompression Sickness,
note: Original USAF survey. Review dates it 1978. The scanned proceedings page carries a handwritten 1980 annotation. The exposure periods are explicit.

title: USAF Experience with Hyperbaric Therapy of Altitude Decompression Sickness (1941–1999)
note: The primary title page also credits Larry P. Krock. The two earlier treatment series are reprinted. Exposure-source percentages in the prose differ from the tabulated counts in the first two periods.

title: The effect of exercise and rest duration on the generation of venous gas bubbles at altitude
note: Twenty volunteers in a crossover. Use participants as the denominator across all conditions. The abstract does not report the number of completed chamber sessions.

title: Decompression to altitude: assumptions, experimental evidence, and future directions
Protective Mechanisms in Hypobaric Decompression
note: Thirteen volunteers in a mechanistic NIRS experiment. The clinical DCS comparisons refer to earlier NASA prebreathe trials.

title: Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging Anomalies in U-2 Pilots with Neurological Decompression Sickness
note: Selected imaging series of U-2 pilots with neurological DCS following aviation exposures. No chamber-exposure denominator.

title: The effectiveness of ground level oxygen treatment for altitude decompression sickness in human research subjects
note: AFRL research archive. Two hours of ground-level oxygen was given to a selected subset.

title: Exercise‐induced altitude decompression sickness
note: Thirty-two male participants received four exercise protocols at individually selected symptom-free resting altitudes, 20,000 to 29,500 ft.

title: Relationship between age and susceptibility to altitude decompression sickness
note: Existing v1.3 lead. The printed title omits decompression. The paper reports 1,299 exposures and shows age-specific findings graphically. No exact age-bin event counts transferred.

title: Mobility of an Elastic Glove for Extravehicular Activity Without Prebreathing
note: Local glove pressure and hand mobility experiment in ten volunteers. No whole-body chamber DCS endpoint.

title: Exercise‐enhanced preoxygenation increases protection from decompression sickness
note: Matched profiles within 26 volunteers. Table VI has four not-accomplished cells. The printed V means severe VGE (Spencer grades 3 or 4). A blank symptom field records the table annotation only.

title: Gender not a factor for altitude decompression sickness risk
note: DTIC archive of the authors’ manuscript, cross-checked with PMID 12546293. The comparison includes 859 of 961 exposures. The treatment paragraph uses its own denominators.

title: The effect of exposure to 35,000 ft on incidence of altitude decompression sickness
note: Public copy of the published article. Table I gives 91% DCS during mild exercise, whereas the Discussion says 94%. Table I is used.

title: Oxygen Consumption at Altitude as a Risk Factor for Altitude Decompression Sickness
note: Already curated as v1/webb10. Workload was reconstructed at ground level and the DCS outcomes refer to historical groups.

title: Altitude decompression sickness susceptibility: Influence of anthropometric and physiologic variables
note: Selected repeat volunteers in the AFRL archive. This differs from the v1.3 Webb 2005 altitude-series paper. Primary Results report 35/240 in the lowest subject/study ratio bin. This is a relative index, not a clinical event count.

title: Moderate exercise after altitude exposure fails to induce decompression sickness
note: Figure 1 includes all 67 volunteers. Seven required treatment or referral before randomization. Figure 1, Table III and Results give 31 assigned to exercise. Table I anthropometry labels the exercise group 30.

title: An abrupt zero‐preoxygenation altitude threshold for decompression sickness symptoms
note: Already curated in v1.4 as webb98. Curve-based predicted thresholds and historical comparator rows are distinguished in that release.
